reasoning_traces.think:
The core tension lies between marginal and conditional coverage guarantees in conformal prediction. The marginal guarantee (eq. 1) ensures coverage over all possible calibration sets, but in practice, models are calibrated once and reused. This leads to a critical failure mode: conditional coverage can be arbitrarily poor even when marginal coverage appears acceptable. The critique highlights that small calibration sets (e.g., m=10) can cause conditional coverage to fall below 85% with high probability. The conditional bound (eq. 3) provides a probabilistic guarantee over calibration set draws, showing that for small m, the probability of meeting the nominal coverage drops sharply. This implies that in GSE’s context, where calibration sets may be limited (e.g., historical game data), relying solely on marginal coverage leads to false confidence. Thus, GSE must adopt a resampling-based QC protocol that monitors conditional coverage distributions and enforces recalibration when thresholds are crossed.
